99.speaker: Lileas Graf

114.speaker: Denis Stahler
114.text: "I am grateful to the President for finally paving the way for my party into Assembly. But I ask you: Why stop there? Sordish Socialism is upon our doorstep. All that is left to do is embrace it."
114.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Debate_DenisChallenge"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Law_Threshold_3"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Law_Threshold_8"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Debate_Enable_DenisStahler"] == false) == false)

136.speaker: Player

137.speaker: Player

138.speaker: Player

139.speaker: Moderator

144.text: "Whatever differences President Rayne and I expressed during this debate, our alliance still stands. No matter who wins, we will govern together to bring Sordland a freedom it has never known before."

164.text: "No. The charade has gone on long enough. How can the blatant censorship of the media go unremarked upon on this stage?"

166.speaker: Narrator

168.speaker: Denis Stahler
168.text: "Admiration? You had me thrown in prison!"

172.speaker: Player
172.text: "Denis, I have nothing but admiration for you and your ideology. Please do not test my goodwill."

174.speaker: Denis Stahler
174.text: "This charade has gone on long enough. Can't you others see he has the media rigged against us?"

192.speaker: Player
192.text: "Mr. Stahler. If I really am as powerful as you claim, wouldn't it be extremely foolish of you to speak against me?"

194.speaker: Player
194.text: "Mr. Stahler. Leave this stage and do not ever show your face in front of me again."

200.speaker: Player
200.text: "I have no idea what you're talking about."

202.speaker: Denis Stahler
202.text: "Abdicating responsibility. A good look for a President."

203.speaker: Player
203.text: "If I was censoring the media, would I permit you to make this kind of scene?"

204.speaker: Player
204.text: "Whatever you think you know about me, it's a lie."

205.speaker: Narrator
205.text: Denis gaped at me indignantly, then sat, his face red.

206.speaker: Player
206.text: "Guards, this man is a danger to me. Please escort him out of the building at once."

210.speaker: Narrator
210.text: Denis sat, his face red. None of the other candidates spoke.

212.speaker: Denis Stahler
212.text: "I won't play this game a second longer."

216.speaker: Narrator
216.text: He and Denis walked out of the studio. None of the other candidates spoke.

224.speaker: Denis Stahler
224.text: "They're more violent than they used to be, I'll agree with you there. But your reaction crossed a line."

226.speaker: Player
226.text: "The Red Youth were out of control. You should have done something."

228.speaker: Mansoun Leke
228.text: "It doesn't have to be this way. Vote People's Front for real change in '57."

230.speaker: Narrator
230.text: Denis loudly pushed his chair back and stormed out of the studio. None of the other candidates spoke.

231.speaker: Denis Stahler
231.text: "Let's just get this dog and pony show over with."

232.speaker: Mansoun Leke
232.text: "Sorry, Denis, I can't risk it. You're on your own."

233.speaker: Narrator
233.text: Mansoun got up and looked into the camera.

240.speaker: Denis Stahler
240.text: "You claimed to understand the plight of the common man back in Narbel. But it was all an act, wasn't it, Mr. President?"

241.speaker: Denis Stahler
241.text: "Ever since our confrontation in Narbel I've known exactly what kind of man you were, Mr. President."
